article.title: Ousted Bangladesh PM's Daughter Steps Down as WHO Regional Chief after Fraud Probe
article.summary: Saima Wazed, daughter of ousted Bangladeshi leader Sheikh Hasina, has resigned as the WHO’s Southeast Asia regional director after an extended internal investigation into alleged financial fraud and academic misrepresentation left her unpaid, mentally exhausted, and financially drained.

article.title: Hasina’s daughter resigns as WHO regional head
article.summary: NEW DELHI: Saima Wazed, the World Health Organisation’s Southeast Asia head and daughter of ousted Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, resigned on Wednesday, according to her resignation letter, following fraud investigations by the UN agency and Bangladeshi authorities.Wazed’s case shows how the fallout from Hasina’sousterfollowing a deadly uprising against her around mid-2024 has spread to her family members, beyond her political allies. Many of Hasina’s allies face criminal charges, including for alleged corruption in Bangladesh, or live in self-imposed exile like Hasina.In a statement on Thursday, the WHO said a committee had recommended Wazed’s dismissal the day before her resignation. The UN health agency had placed Wazed, who took office as its Southeast Asia regional director in early 2024 for a five-year term, on unpaid administrative leave late last year. article.title: Sheikh Hasina's daughter Saima Wazed resigns as WHO regional head after fraud allegations: What to know
article.summary: Saima Wazed, daughter of ousted Bangladesh PM Sheikh Hasina, resigned as WHO Southeast Asia regional director after fraud investigations by the UN agency and Bangladesh authorities. Wazed, who denies the allegations, had been on unpaid leave since 2025.
